Title: Driver in fatal Gua Musang crash believed to be migrant smuggler
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Police believe the driver of a Proton X70 involved in a crash that killed two people on Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis near Bukit Lanjut on Thursday was a migrant smuggler.
District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the driver, who was critically injured in the crash, is now in a coma and receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital.
He said the incident occurred when the driver, who was travelling from Kota Baru towards Kuala Lumpur, spotted a police roadblock and suddenly made a
U-turn
in an attempt to escape.
"The driver appeared to have spotted the roadblock before making a U-turn and attempting to flee.
"He subsequently lost control of the Proton X70, causing it to crash," he said.
Sik said the vehicle was believed to have been carrying eight undocumented migrants at the time of the incident.
He said two migrants were killed while six others were injured.
"The undocumented migrants were taken to hospital for treatment, while the driver is in critical condition and remains in a coma," he said.
Sik said police were investigating the case under Section 55E and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Sections 186 and 353 of the Penal Code.
Section 55E of the Immigration Act involves harbouring undocumented migrants, while Section 6(1)(c) concerns offences involving illegal entry into Malaysia.
Sections 186 and 353 of the Penal Code relate to obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties and using criminal force against a public servant, respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal authorities begin burying 229 unidentified bodies after floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities in Nepal's Chitwan district began burying 229 unidentified bodies on Saturday due to public health risks from decomposition, following Wednesday's devastating floods in Rasuwa.
The District Security Committee said 233 bodies had been recovered from the disaster so far, of which only four had been identified.
The bodies and human remains recovered from riverbanks and kept at various facilities had decomposed to the point that visual identification was no longer possible, it said, according to
The Kathmandu Post.
Health experts have warned that further decomposition and the foul odour from the remains could increase the risk of infections and disease outbreaks.
The committee decided on Saturday to bury all the unidentified and unclaimed bodies under the Unidentified and Unclaimed Bodies Management (First Amendment) Directive, 2026, as an emergency measure to prevent further decomposition and ensure their safe, dignified and lawful disposal.
DNA samples will be collected from all the bodies before burial and records will be maintained using identification numbers, according to the decision.
The burial site is an open area in Devghat, Ward 1, of Bharatpur Metropolitan City.
Anil Thapa, an inspector with Chitwan police, said each body had been assigned a unique identification number, with a tag attached to a steel plate, so that relatives could exhume the remains once a DNA match is confirmed.

Title: Nepal disaster: Families of Malaysians still unaccounted for to receive briefing tomorrow
Article:
SEREMBAN: Families of Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border will be briefed by the Foreign Ministry, National Security Council (NSC) and relevant agencies tomorrow.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the meeting would provide the latest updates on efforts to locate the Malaysians who remain unaccounted for.
"If the families wish to go to Nepal, we will try to arrange their travel. However, access to the site or ground zero is difficult due to communication problems and damaged bridges," he told reporters after the Ziarah Kasih programme at Taman Kelab Tuanku, Mambau, here this evening.
He said Wisma Putra was operating a 24-hour operations room to monitor developments following the disaster and remained in constant contact with Nepal's Foreign Ministry, NSC and relevant agencies.
He also said the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu was providing him with daily updates, while additional staff had been deployed to assist Malaysians affected by the disaster.
"Many of those previously categorised as missing have now been contacted. The Chinese authorities said several people on their side of the border have also been reached, but we have yet to confirm their nationality," he said.
Mohamad said Nepal did not require foreign search and rescue (SAR) teams, based on its experience managing SAR operations following the Kathmandu earthquake several years ago.
Instead, Nepal had asked countries wishing to help to provide financial contributions to support relief efforts, he said.
"They do need financial contributions. Even the World Bank has issued a statement offering assistance to Nepal," he said.
Mohamad said representatives from his office and officers from the operations room would also attend a media meeting with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in Kuala Lumpur tomorrow to answer questions and provide further updates on Malaysians who remain unaccounted for.

Title: 11,060 Sahabat Madani volunteers join nationwide movement
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A total of 11,060 Sahabat Madani volunteers have registered nationwide, forming a volunteer movement aimed at strengthening community ties and encouraging Malaysians from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds to serve together.
In a statement today, the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister's Department (ICU JPM) said the network focuses on community services that provide direct benefits, including supporting vulnerable groups, helping children who have dropped out of school, creating career and business opportunities for young people, and providing aid during times of crisis.
"The spirit of reform is put into practice through Sahabat Madani by building a national network that brings together the government, volunteers and communities, with a focus on action, transparency and delivering results for the people.
"Through well-organised, inclusive and responsive coordination, services and interventions are provided according to communities' actual needs, helping to broaden the benefits of development, strengthen community capacity and ensure no one is left behind," it said.
Earlier, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim launched the national Sahabat Madani initiative at the Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani 2026 highlight programme at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Permatang Pauh here.
As Malaysia marks National Day, ICU JPM said the spirit of independence was reflected not only in flying the Jalur Gemilang, but also in the willingness of Malaysians to serve, uphold integrity and help those in need.
It said volunteer work across social differences could promote harmony and strengthen community ties, while bringing people together to tackle poverty, hardship, corruption and injustice.
Under the "Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" aspiration of shared wellbeing, Sahabat Madani aims to encourage care, responsibility and active participation across society.
ICU JPM also urged young people to reject divisive sentiments and use their skills and expertise to contribute to the country's progress, helping build a society united through service and harmony.

Title: Selangor looks to AI to boost govt services, efficiency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor is moving towards becoming an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered state, with AI set to be integrated into government operations and public services to improve efficiency.
State Islamic Affairs and Digital Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the next phase of the state's Smart City agenda would focus on using data and AI to shape policies and improve services.
"Selangor completed 60 initiatives under its Smart City programme from 2016 to 2025, including the integration of applications and systems to monitor public assistance, as well as digital platforms for city management.
"Under the Second Selangor Plan 2026-2030, we will move towards AI Cities, a leap that Selangor will try to lead."
Fahmi said the move would complete the Smart City cycle by allowing data collected through existing systems and applications to be analysed and translated into policies, regulations and guidelines.
"A city will become truly smart if data can be analysed and translated into policies, regulations and guidelines that are more appropriate for implementation."
He said AI-powered systems would be used in government processes and public services by 2030, although the extent of implementation was still being explored.
"I am optimistic that Selangor will have AI systems of this kind in use next year."
[[nid:1521394]]
Fahmi said the state needed more efficient ways to manage its services, with about 19,000 civil servants serving a state he described as 11 times larger than Singapore.
He said AI could help automate government processes, analyse large amounts of data and provide faster guidance on the action required.
The development of an AI City would require centralised digital infrastructure capable of collecting, storing and analysing data using graphics processing units and the latest AI technology.
Fahmi said Selangor's 5G coverage, which stood at 97 per cent, would also provide an important foundation for the initiative.
Among the applications being explored are AI-powered chatbots and agents that could provide round-the-clock access to government services, reducing the need for people to rely on social media or visit government offices.
Fahmi said the state was also developing 'Teduh' facilities for p-hailing riders, with all local authorities expected to have one by the end of this year.
The facilities are designed to provide riders with a safe and comfortable place to rest while waiting for orders, with amenities including closed-circuit television, seating, fans, charging ports and prayer facilities.
"The facilities will also serve as data collection points for the state government to better understand and safeguard the welfare of p-hailing riders.
"The initiative is being developed through collaboration between the state government, local authorities, p-hailing companies and agencies including the Road Transport Department and police," Fahmi said.
He added that Selangor was also exploring a Low Altitude Economy, including the use of drones for monitoring, delivery services and testing new drone technologies.
He said the state was establishing the Selangor Drone Port 1000 at Universiti Selangor as a centre of excellence to explore policies and regulations governing the safe use of drones below 1,000m.

Title: Rescuers push deeper into mudslide-hit areas at Xizang border post
Article:
GYIRONG: Drones are scouting conditions as rescue teams advance on foot following a massive mudslide in Gyirong Port, southwest China's Xizang Region, where blocked roads and the risk of further disasters are hampering the search for hundreds of missing people, reported Xinhua.
As of 1am on Saturday, seven people had been confirmed dead and 554 others remained missing at the port on the China-Nepal border, according to Xizang's emergency management department.
"We will race against time to search for every missing person and will not give up any hope," an official with a frontline working group of the Emergency Management Ministry (MEM) said on Saturday.
The official said rescuers are pushing deeper into the disaster zone while authorities step up monitoring of secondary-disaster risks and work to keep emergency communications running.
[[nid:1521390]]
The National Fire and Rescue Administration has deployed 681 personnel, 13 rescue dogs, 113 vehicles, 47 drones and specialised equipment. Two teams comprising 17 personnel have also been sent to establish monitoring posts.
Advance teams are moving towards the affected area by land and water, with heavy-lift drones also being used to transport supplies. Twenty-one rescuers have so far reached the border gate at Gyirong Port, the official said.
MEM has also deployed 60 personnel and 28 pieces of equipment from a natural disaster rescue centre operated by China Anneng Group.
Two unmanned aerial vehicles have been deployed to provide uninterrupted emergency communications.
The working group has also coordinated inspections and repairs of communications lines, with one base station restored and three new ones added.
Military, civilian and commercial satellite resources have been mobilised to monitor the disaster site and surrounding areas.
Meanwhile, the Natural Resources Ministry, Water Resources Ministry, China Earthquake Administration and relevant research institutions are monitoring and issuing early warnings for risks including ice-rock avalanches, secondary mudslides and landslides.
China and Nepal are "in close communication and coordinating efforts" on search and rescue operations, China's Foreign Ministry said.
The emergency management official said the frontline working group would focus on three priorities: conducting scientific search and rescue operations, with additional specialised teams and equipment deployed as needed; strengthening monitoring and early warnings for secondary disasters using radar, satellites, drones and on-site equipment; and providing guidance on disaster relief and assistance to affected residents.
The working group, together with the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, has allocated 30,000 central government disaster-relief items, including tents, heating stoves, clothing, quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats.
It has also coordinated donations of more than 50,000 emergency supplies, including food and drinking water, and worked with the Red Cross Society of China to allocate another 2,500 items, including tents and quilts.
– Bernama-Xinhua

Title: Maha 2026: Exhibition Hall A reopens after smoke incident
Article:
SERDANG: Exhibition Hall A at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) reopened this evening after being temporarily closed following an incident involving smoke and an unpleasant smell.
In a statement, the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 organising committee said the incident at 4.50pm was brought under control after checks by the Fire and Rescue Department and the site's safety management team found no ongoing safety threat.
"The organiser wishes to emphasise that the technical incident was resolved without any structural implications.
"No injuries, medical emergencies or fatalities were reported. Exhibition Hall A has been declared safe and reopened to visitors with immediate effect," it said.
The committee said the temporary evacuation of the hall was a standard precautionary measure under the Maha 2026 Safety Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) to ensure the safety and comfort of visitors and exhibitors.
Maha 2026 is being held at Maeps from Aug 28 to Sept 6, involving about 2,000 exhibitors and targeting more than 4 million visitors.

Title: Traffic flow on major highways congested following long weekend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic flow on several major highways in the country was slow and congested as of 6 pm this evening due to the increase in vehicles following the school holidays and National Day holiday which begins this weekend.
A spokesman for the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) said traffic heading north was detected moving slowly from Sungai Buloh towards Bukit Beruntung, Bukit Tagar to Lembah Beringin, and Sungkai to Simpang Pulai.
He said congestion to the north was also reported from Changkat Jering to Taiping Utara, Bukit Merah to Bandar Baharu and Permatang Pauh towards Bertam.
"Meanwhile, southbound traffic flow was reported to be congested starting from Bangi towards Southville, and continuing from Nilai Utara extending to Pedas Linggi.
"For the route towards the East Coast, traffic was detected to be slow starting from the Gombak toll lapza towards Genting Sempah and from Lentang towards Bentong, in addition to some congestion from Lanchang to Temerloh following flood mitigation repair works," he said.
The congestion trend is similar to that of festive holidays due to the number of vehicles recorded increasing drastically since yesterday evening and early this morning, according to a spokesman.
He expected this high and slow traffic flow to continue until late tonight as people took the opportunity to go on holiday and return to their hometowns.
Meanwhile, traffic flow on the West Coast Expressway (WCE) was reported to be still under control and smooth in both directions so far.
In this regard, MHA advised highway users to plan your journey as the driving time is expected to be long.
The public is also advised to ensure that their vehicles are well maintained before starting their journey and to always monitor the current traffic status via MHA's official social media platforms or related media.

Title: Haze: Japan offers water-bombing aid as Kalimantan ISPU surges past 1,000
Article:
JAKARTA: Japan has offered Indonesia assistance with water-bombing operations to combat forest and land fires in Kalimantan, as the Air Pollutant Standard Index (ISPU) in the region surged past 1,000.
National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Acting Head of Data, Information and Disaster Communication Centre Berton Panjaitan said the assistance would involve three helicopters, including a Chinook, with operations scheduled to begin on Sept 10.
"Preparations are under way, including a site survey, with discussions focusing on the operational aspects of water-bombing missions in Kalimantan," he said at an online press conference on Saturday.
Latest data from the Environment Ministry showed Jekan Raya in Palangka Raya, Central Kalimantan, recording an ISPU of 1,108 as of 4.55pm on Saturday, while Southeast Pontianak in West Kalimantan reached 1,075. Both readings were categorised as hazardous.
BNPB also reported 9,242 hotspots across West, Central and South Kalimantan, with all three provinces recording increases.
West Kalimantan saw the sharpest rise, with the number of hotspots increasing by 1,629 to 3,371. A total of 171 fire spots were recorded across the three provinces.
Despite the worsening conditions, Berton said weather modification operations had helped bring rain to several affected areas on Sumatra, including parts of Riau, South Sumatra, Jambi and Lampung.
However, similar operations could not be conducted in Central and South Kalimantan due to a lack of suitable clouds.
BNPB currently has 52 aircraft supporting firefighting operations, comprising 38 for water bombing and 14 for aerial patrols and weather modification, with about 3.5 million litres of water dropped across the six priority provinces.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police open investigation paper over post defaming personnel in Puchong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have opened an investigation paper regarding a Facebook post that allegedly contained defamatory statements against police officers at a petrol station in Batu 14, Puchong, Selangor yesterday.
Subang Jaya police chief assistant commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said they received a report from a policeman who was on duty at the time of the incident at 10.54pm.
"The police have opened an investigation paper following the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
"The owner of the account will be traced immediately to assist in the investigation," he said in a statement today.
He said the post uploaded by the owner of the Facebook account using the name 'Izz Fairuzz' was traced after it went viral on social media.
Wan Azlan said the post claimed that a police patrol vehicle blocked traffic while the personnel involved were allegedly waiting for food from a foreign trader at the petrol station without paying.
In this regard, he advised the public not to make any speculation regarding the allegations that went viral on social media.
"The public is requested to give the police full space to conduct further investigations without making any speculation," he said.
He also asked those with information related to the incident to contact the Subang Jaya district police control centre at 03-7862 7100.
He said the identity of the informant would be kept confidential.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM extends condolences to Norway over passing of King Harald V
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended condolences on behalf of the Malaysian government to the people of Norway on the passing of King Harald V.
Anwar said King Harald would be remembered for his generous understanding of what it meant to be Norwegian, including his recognition of the country's diverse society.
"He spoke of a country made up of people whose families came from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Poland and many other places, and affirmed that they, too, were Norwegian.
"His words were a reminder that a nation draws strength from the dignity it accords all its people," he said in a statement via his Facebook,today.
Anwar said King Harald also understood the weight of an oath and the importance of remaining true to one's commitments.
"Malaysia joins the people of Norway in mourning his passing," the prime minister said.
King Harald V died
on Friday at age 89 at the National Hospital in Oslo, after having been hospitalised since Aug 17 and was receiving cortisone treatment for hemolytic anemia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families cling on to hope after Nepal-Tibet border disaster
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hope is fading, but it has not disappeared for the families of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporean travellers still unaccounted for following the Nepal-Tibet border flood disaster on Aug 26.
Among the 75 family members gathered today in Batu Caves was Jamaliah Tengku Ismail, who said she was trying to balance hope with the possibility of bad news about her 68-year-old husband, Wan Nasir Abdul Talib.
"I would say I am still hopeful, but I am resigned to whatever may be the outcome.
"We do not know what the situation is, and as each day passes, the chances become slimmer," the 68-year-old told the New Straits Times during a press conference by the families, who have formed a group, Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH).
Nasir left Kathmandu early in the morning for the Nepal-Tibet border with a close-knit group of friends from his neighbourhood in  Bukit Jelutong, Shah Alam, who had spent months planning the trip.
Jamaliah said he called her during the journey, but she missed the call.
"He called me while he was on the way, but I did not answer. Before leaving, he had sent me a message," she said.
The group was later traced to a cafe, about an hour before the flash floods struck.
Jamaliah said Nasir had been in high spirits the night before and was looking forward to the trip, which he had joined mainly to enjoy the scenery.
She believed Nasir and the others may have reached higher ground or found shelter, particularly as some members of the group had survival training. It is believed some of them are firemen.
"As long as there is no other news, no news is still good news. We have to find them as quickly as possible. That is what matters," she said.
Among those travelling with Nasir was his close friend, 56-year-old Jason Ngeow.
Jason's sister, Joanne Ngeow, 59, said she last saw him about two weeks ago in their hometown in Ipoh. She said her brother, a businessman, was fit, active and accustomed to travelling.
"He is single and rarely tells us what he is up to, but this time he told me he was just going there for a relaxing hike," she said.
Joanne said she was still holding on to hope, but one of her greatest struggles was shielding their elderly parents from the full weight of the news.
"My father is 90 and my mother is in her 80s. They cannot take this kind of news. I kept it from them for two days before my father came to know about it.
"I just told them that there was a communication breakdown and they seemed okay for now."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A Merdeka memory, made for the front page
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Under the scorching afternoon sun at Dataran Merdeka, visitors streamed through the historic square, watching parade rehearsals, taking photographs and soaking up the festivities ahead of National Day.
As crowds moved through the area, a mobile roadshow truck gave them another reason to pause — the chance to see their own faces on the front page of a newspaper.
For Arul Selvan Jeyaraj, 48, from Ipoh, the experience was particularly fitting.
He had come to see the National Day preparations when the Wajah Malaysia photobooth caught his attention. Given a choice of newspapers for his personalised front page, he picked the New Straits Times.
"NST is still a paper that I physically read.
"I still buy a copy and read it every other day, so it is a nice touch," he said.
[[nid:1521351]]
Arul described seeing himself on the front page as "a really good feeling".
He also hoped the novelty could help draw younger Malaysians towards newspapers.
"Many people don't read newspapers anymore. Everybody is more into social media.
"I hope this will encourage them to start reading physical or online newspapers.
"It is good to know what is going on in the country and the world," he said.
[[nid:1521350]]
Meanwhile, for Sanjeevan Sivaraj, 36, from Gelugor, Penang, discovering the campaign turned a family holiday into an unexpected Merdeka memory.
He had travelled to the capital with his wife and their two young children for a family holiday, unaware of the festivities taking place at Dataran Merdeka.
"We saw the photobooth and thought it looked interesting, so we wanted to have a picture," he said.
Sanjeevan, who mostly reads news online, said holding a physical newspaper again — this time with his family's photograph on the front page — reminded him of the experience of reading print.
"It is actually very good. It is also a reminder to sometimes buy a newspaper and read it," he said.
His children, he said, had been learning about National Day and singing Merdeka songs at school, while their visit to Dataran Merdeka gave them a chance to experience the celebrations themselves.
"I am proud to be born in Malaysia and to have people of different races living here in harmony," he said.
Meanwhile, Nurshazwana Izzlyen Kamaruzaman, 25, from Selayang, said the campaign offered a different experience for a generation more accustomed to screens than newsprint.
"Sometimes, children have never even held a newspaper. When we give it to them, they are like, 'Wow, is this what a newspaper is like? I can read it.'
"This gives them the chance to experience it," she said.
Nurshazwana, who also won a Merdeka-themed Kahoot quiz at the event, said the questions took participants through Malaysia's journey from independence to the present day.
"They asked many questions about Merdeka, from the beginning of our independence until now, things that, as Malaysians, we should know," she said.
She said putting ordinary Malaysians at the centre of Wajah Malaysia was fitting for the celebrations.
"It is a really good idea because we want to celebrate the Malaysian people.
"They want to gather Malaysians from different backgrounds, bring out that spirit and put their faces on billboards, television and newspapers," she said.
The Wajah Malaysia mobile roadshow truck, stationed at Dataran Merdeka alongside Festival Ambang Merdeka 2026, houses a photobooth where visitors can have their photographs featured on personalised mock front pages of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian or Harian Metro.
A collaboration between the NSTP Marketing Department and Media Prima Group Marketing, the campaign will take its mobile roadshow truck to the Petronas Twin Towers early tomorrow morning.

Title: GRS to continue cooperation with PH, BN, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) will continue its cooperation with its existing allies, said its chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
"Currently, the Sabah state government is led by GRS. Within GRS, there are several component parties. The government is also made up of Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN), and they are already part of the government.
"For now, we will continue our cooperation with the parties that are currently part of the state government," he told the media after chairing the Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (Gagasan) supreme council meeting here.
Hajiji, who is also Gagasan president, was responding to questions from reporters on possible alliances in the upcoming general election.
When asked about the allocation of the 25 parliamentary seats among GRS and its partners, Hajiji said GRS, which leads the state government, would negotiate with its partners and hoped they would be rational in the distribution of seats.
However, the chief minister said no discussions had taken place so far.
"Although we do not know when the general election will be held, the term runs until the end of next year.
"We must be prepared from now, mobilising the party at all levels, including the wings, by going down to the ground and organising programmes to prepare for the general election.
"We will continue working on the ground and meeting the people to strengthen the machinery of GRS and its component parties."
Meanwhile, on the recent announcement by Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) that it was withdrawing its support, Hajiji said the party was not part of
GRS
.
"There is no issue of it withdrawing support or anything like that. What is important here is that KDM has one elected representative in Paginatan (Datuk Rusdin Riman), who has expressed support for the state government.
"His party may be KDM, but what is important is the support in the state legislative assembly."
Earlier, Hajiji announced 25 divisional chiefs, including four new faces in Kota Marudu, Putatan, Kalabakan and Semporna.

Title: Anwar: Learn English, Chinese, Tamil beyond mastering Bahasa Melayu
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said proficiency in Bahasa Melayu should remain essential for Malaysians, while learning other languages could open up greater educational and economic opportunities.
Speaking at the Sahabat Madani 2026 Merdeka Eve programme at UiTM Permatang Pauh here today, Anwar said Malaysians should not regard the development of other languages and cultures as a threat to national identity.
He said Malaysians should be encouraged to learn English, Chinese, Tamil and other languages while maintaining proficiency in Bahasa Melayu.
"We must be proficient in Bahasa Melayu, but we can also learn English, Chinese, Tamil and other languages," he said.
He said Malaysia's diversity should instead be regarded as a strength, with Malaysians sharing a common aspiration to elevate the country's standing.
Anwar said national unity did not mean abandoning the identity or rights of any community, but bringing Malaysians together around shared values, humanity and a commitment to national progress.
He also urged Malaysians to reject racial and communal divisions, saying disputes over race, skin colour and ethnicity could distract the nation from addressing issues affecting everyone, including corruption, abuse of power, poverty and inequality.
"If we are still being divided and allowed to fight over race, skin colour and other issues, we cannot move towards national development," he said.
Anwar stressed that corruption and abuse of power should never be viewed through a racial lens, arguing that those entrusted with public office must be held accountable regardless of their background.
"Whether the person who steals is Malay, Chinese, Indian, Iban or Kadazan, there is no difference," he said, adding that the country must be governed with courage, integrity and accountability.
Anwar said Malaysia's constitutional foundations, including Islam as the religion of the Federation, the position of Bahasa Melayu, the special position of Malays and Bumiputera, and the institution of the Malay rulers, should be upheld.
He also called on young Malaysians to move beyond the divisions of the past and develop a new outlook based on knowledge, integrity and courage.
He said the younger generation had a crucial role in ensuring Malaysia remained peaceful, stable and capable of competing globally.
"This is a great nation," he said, urging young Malaysians to honour the sacrifices of previous generations by ensuring independence continued to have meaning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kopmedia ranks among KL's top 50 cooperatives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Koperasi Media Prima Bhd (Kopmedia) has been ranked 46th among the 50 best-performing cooperatives in the Federal Territory under the 2026 Majlis Apresiasi Gerakan Koperasi Wilayah Persekutuan (MAGK'26).
The recognition was presented by the Malaysia Cooperative Societies Commission (SKM) Federal Territory branch at the appreciation ceremony on Aug 27.
A total of 55 cooperatives received recognition at the event, comprising the 50 best cooperatives, two premier cooperatives and three special award recipients.
The awards were assessed based on both non-financial and financial factors.
This included compliance with prevailing legislation, governance, contributions to members, revenue, asset ownership and fund accumulation.
Cooperatives were also evaluated based on their financial management practices and adherence to good governance.
SKM chairman Lieutenant General (R) Datuk Ahmad Norihan Jalal said the cooperative movement in the Federal Territory could be regarded as the backbone of Malaysia's cooperative movement, with 35 of the country's 100 best cooperatives based in the territory.
He said five of the seven premier cooperatives were also from the Federal Territory, while 80 of the 1,200 cooperatives in the territory recorded annual income exceeding RM5 million and were categorised as large-cluster cooperatives.
"Therefore, I believe the focus of cooperatives in the Federal Territory is somewhat different compared with cooperatives in the smaller states, with greater emphasis being placed on business expansion," he said in his speech at the ceremony.
The recognition comes as the cooperative sector in the Federal Territory recorded growth across several key indicators in 2025.
The number of cooperatives increased to 1,223 in 2025 from 1,214 a year earlier, while total membership rose 5.69 per cent to 2.51 million.
Total assets grew 9.82 per cent to RM24.65 billion, while total revenue increased 4.92 per cent to RM7.46 billion during the year.

Title: Families of 49 Malaysians, three Singaporeans missing in Nepal-China flood disaster plead for answers [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 72 hours of silence and uncertainty over the fate of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporeans accounted for following the Nepal-China border flood disaster has left their families in anguish.
The families, represented by Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH), are pleading for daily official updates and stronger engagement with foreign authorities as none of their loved ones had been accounted for through official reports.
The group said that it represented families of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporeans travelling in three separate groups whose whereabouts remained unknown.
They said their loved ones were not among the 38 Malaysians Wisma Putra had reportedly said yesterday that it had established contact with.
In its latest update issued today, Wisma Putra said 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on Aug 26.
MASFIH said the 52 travellers the families are highlighting comprise 23 Malaysians and three Singaporeans travelling with Leaf Holiday, nine Malaysians linked to the Dream Tibet Travel and Tours group, and 17 Malaysians travelling with Fishtail Tours and Travels.
Speaking on behalf of the families, Dr R Manivannan, whose sister is among those unaccounted for, said every hour without reliable information was worsening their anxiety.
"This is not a normal missing-person situation. Every hour without reliable information increases the anxiety, suffering and emotional distress faced by the families," he said in a press conference at a restaurant in Batu Caves, Selangor, here today.
He said the group was appealing to Wisma Putra and the Malaysian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing to provide daily official updates, even when there were no new verified developments.
The families also want liaison officers to communicate directly with three MASFIH representatives, saying a centralised channel would reduce confusion and prevent relatives from having to contact multiple agencies for information.
Manivannan said some families had experienced difficulty contacting or receiving responses from the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu over the past two days, while acknowledging that diplomatic missions were operating under difficult circumstances.
"We are not blaming anyone. This is a plea for a more effective communication structure in dealing with an extraordinary humanitarian crisis," he said.
MASFIH also urged Putrajaya to use diplomatic channels with Nepal and China to seek approval for the deployment of Malaysian search-and-rescue personnel and other relevant expertise to assist efforts to locate those still missing.
The group said information on search-and-rescue efforts had largely come from the Nepalese side, while families had received little or no direct information on developments in Tibet or China.
The group urged Malaysian authorities to obtain verified information from Beijing on search operations, survivors, casualties and any Malaysians who may have been located on the Tibetan side of the border.
Manivannan said the families were not being confrontational but simply seeking answers, coordination and action.
"For families waiting for news of their loved ones, silence without information is deeply painful. Every hour matters, every life matters and every family deserves answers," he added.
The disaster struck Nepal's Rasuwa district near the Tibet border on Aug 26, when flash floods and landslides swept through the Rasuwagadhi area, damaging roads and infrastructure and cutting off communications.
The floods affected both sides of the Nepal-China border, with thousands later reported missing across the wider disaster zone as search-and-rescue operations continued in difficult terrain.

Title: Street artist keeps old KL alive through Merdeka memories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As the Ambang Merdeka Festival 2026 approaches this weekend near historic Dataran Merdeka, street artist Mahadzir Jam is preserving memories of an older Kuala Lumpur through his art.
The 57-year-old, who has spent nearly four decades working in the capital, remembers when roads that now run one way carried traffic in both directions and when the Sultan Abdul Samad Building served as a courthouse.
As the city has transformed, Mahadzir, from Selayang, has continued capturing scenes of traditional Malaysia through his art.
Using acrylic markers, he paints colourful landscapes of traditional village houses, coconut trees and greenery on small canvases, magnets and other souvenirs, many marked "Kuala Lumpur" for tourists seeking a keepsake from the capital.
"Kuala Lumpur has changed a lot.
"You can see it from the infrastructure," he told the New Straits Times.
Mahadzir began working at Central Market around 1989 and spent more than three decades there before the Covid-19 pandemic and high rental costs during the movement control order forced him and other traders to leave.
He remembers Central Market as resembling a wet market when he first started there.
"When I first started there (Central Market), it was like a fish market.
"Now it is a proper complex. It is beautiful and the crowds are bigger," he said.
Two months ago, he found a new spot beneath the trees near Dataran Merdeka.
From about 10am, he lays out his hand-painted canvases, magnets and keychains, working largely freehand as tourists and visitors pass through the historic district.
"My business relies entirely on tourists. That is why I write 'Kuala Lumpur' a lot and paint scenes of old villages," he said.
His landscapes come largely from imagination, shaped by decades of painting and memories of a Malaysia that has changed with each passing National Day.
He said today's tourists preferred simplicity.
"They just want originality. They want the piece to have the artist's signature, that's all," said Mahadzir.
He has recently seen tourists from China and Italy, while weekends and major events draw Malaysians from across the Klang Valley and beyond.
"When there is an event at Dataran Merdeka, many locals come.
"During the day, it is mostly tourists, but at night, it gets very busy with locals," he said.
With National Day celebrations approaching, Mahadzir expects more visitors and hopes the occasion will bring continued attention to the capital's historic landmarks and small traders.
"When there are many tourists, our economy is doing quite well. If there aren't tourists, it means people don't want to come to Malaysia.
"If the country is stable, they will come," he said.
The street has also given him a community.
Fellow artists, security guards, street sweepers and DBKL workers have become familiar faces, with some watching his belongings when he steps away to eat or pray.
"I know a lot of people here. The street sweepers and even the DBKL workers who look after the trees become friends," he said.
After decades of watching Kuala Lumpur evolve, Mahadzir's National Day hope is for the city and Malaysia to be cared for, so future generations can continue to experience the places and stories that shaped the nation.
"For this Merdeka Day, I hope that whatever government is in power takes care of this city of Kuala Lumpur," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar vows to put rakyat's wellbeing ahead of personal gain
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would continue prioritising the wellbeing of the rakyat if given the opportunity to lead the country.
Speaking at the Sahabat Madani 2026 Merdeka Eve programme at UiTM Permatang Pauh here today, Anwar said his focus was to ensure Malaysia remained stable while improving the lives and prospects of its people.
He said the responsibility of leadership was not to enrich oneself, but to use power and public resources responsibly for the benefit of the rakyat.
"I only aspire to ensure the country remains politically stable and peaceful, and to encourage the people, especially the young, to grow and develop their nation," he said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he remained firm in rejecting corruption, abuse of power and attempts to use positions of authority for personal gain.
He said some had approached him with the attitude that holding the posts of prime minister and finance minister presented an opportunity that should be seized.
"There are people who tell me, 'You are already the PM. You are also the finance minister. If you don't take it, when will you?' I say no'.
"I am rather strict when it comes to this. I cannot accept people entrusted with managing agencies, ministries or institutions using their power to cheat," he added.
Anwar said money lost through mismanagement, abuse and corruption could instead be channelled towards addressing the needs of Malaysians, particularly in education and improving the welfare of disadvantaged groups.
He said the country's resources were not meant to be plundered by a select few, stressing that Malaysia was not a poor country.
Instead, better governance and the elimination of leakages could free up resources to be channelled back to the people, students and public institutions, he said.
He said upholding integrity was particularly important in giving meaning to independence, as Malaysians had fought for generations to regain control over their own affairs and national resources.
Anwar also urged young Malaysians to see independence as a continuing responsibility to build a stronger, more united and dignified nation.
He said Malaysia's future depended on a generation that was courageous, principled and committed to improving the dignity and wellbeing of all Malaysians, regardless of race or background.
Leadership, he added, must ultimately be judged by its ability to deliver meaningful improvements to the lives of the rakyat rather than the accumulation of personal wealth or power.
"If all young Malaysians make that commitment, yes, we will deliver," he said.

Title: PH ready to begin Melaka seat talks with BN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is ready to begin seat negotiations with Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka election, but talks are pending several policy decisions at the Umno and BN central level.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said he had been in contact with Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who told him he was awaiting the decisions before proceeding with the discussions.
"When Rauf is ready. I have actually been in contact with him.
"He said he is waiting for several policy decisions at the Umno and BN central level before continuing the discussions," he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita programme with the Ampang Jaya community here today.
His remarks come after Amirudin previously said
PH could finalise its position
on electoral cooperation with BN in the Melaka election before Malaysia Day on Sept 16.
The Selangor menteri besar said PH remained open to negotiations and urged both sides to approach the discussions with sincerity.
He said PH had previously demonstrated its willingness to compromise, including allowing BN to contest some seats won by PH in Selangor.
"We were sincere in our discussions. In fact, we were willing to share areas that we had won in Selangor. That shows our honesty in negotiations," he said.
Asked whether PH would consider contesting seats beyond the 21 constituencies it is expected to target in Melaka, Amirudin said those were seats PH should contest, but he did not want to make an early decision before negotiations began.
"They are the seats that we should contest, but we will see how the discussions go.
"We have not started negotiations yet, so I do not want to make an early decision."
Amirudin also urged political parties not to impose conditions before negotiations begin, saying cooperation would be difficult if a party insisted on contesting only seats it had previously lost.
"Don't put conditions before negotiations. If you say you only want to contest places you lost, it will be difficult," he said.
He said political parties needed to be prepared for various possibilities, adding that any cooperation should be based on sincerity and a clear commitment to maintaining the stability and prosperity achieved under the unity government.
Amirudin said the unity government was formed following the political instability that emerged after the Sheraton Move, adding that such divisions should not be repeated.
"We do not want to repeat that, and we need to establish a stable government," he said.
Yesterday, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said Umno state leaders had been given the green light to hold talks with political parties on possible cooperation in upcoming elections.
However, Asyraf said
any agreement must be based on sincerity and trust
.
The Melaka state assembly's five-year term will end in December 2026, with its dissolution and the state election expected as early as September.
BN won 21 of the 28 state seats in the last Melaka election and initially governed alone before inviting PH into the state administration to mirror the unity coalition at the federal level.
The arrangement unravelled in July after PH's five assemblymen resigned and withdrew their support following the BN-led government's passage of a Bill allowing the appointment of up to seven unelected members to the state assembly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Floods: Nepal reverses decision to reject foreign rescue assistance
Article:
MOSCOW: The Nepalese government has reversed its earlier decision to reject assistance from other countries in rescue operations following devastating floods that claimed hundreds of lives, amid "pressure" from other states, according to the
Kathmandu Post
newspaper, citing a senior government official, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
On Friday, Nepalese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lok Bahadur Chhetri said
Nepal did not need foreign assistance
for search and rescue operations following the flooding.
"We received massive pressure from the international community to allow at least search-and-rescue teams and some experts because their citizens have also gone missing in the floods. We are allowing a limited number of experts in certain areas," the official was quoted as saying by the newspaper on Friday.
Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the daily that foreign experts would assist local rescuers in identifying the bodies so that authorities could return them to relatives in a timely manner.
Previously, the United Nations (UN), the European Union (EU) and several countries had provided financial assistance to Nepal amid the destruction caused by the major flooding.
A powerful flow of water rushed into the Bhote Koshi River in mountainous Nepal on Wednesday.
The causes of the major flooding were initially reported to be an earthquake and a subsequent landslide.
However, on Thursday, the United States Geological Survey (USGS) said that the seismic activity was caused by a glacier collapse rather than underground tremors.
According to the latest data, the death toll from the flooding in Nepal has reached 633 people.
– Bernama-Sputnik/RIA Novosti

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Colonial-era laws must go to give true meaning to independence
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Colonial-era laws should be abolished to ensure Malaysia truly gives meaning to its independence, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said a sovereign nation must have the confidence to review laws inherited from its colonial past, particularly those that restrict the freedom and participation of its people.
"Colonial-era laws must be abolished so that this country can give true meaning to independence," he said in his speech at the Sahabat Madani 2026 Merdeka programme at UiTM Permatang Pauh here.
Anwar said independence was not merely about ending foreign rule, but also about reclaiming Malaysians' right to determine their own destiny, systems and future.
"For hundreds of years, we were humiliated. The Portuguese, the Dutch, the British and the Japanese decided for us. They decided for us," he said.
Anwar said the colonial experience demonstrated the true cost of losing sovereignty, with key decisions affecting the country's administration, resources and future being determined by foreign powers.
"Think if you lived at that time. Government officers had British bosses. Policies were decided in London. The country's resources were decided in London. That is the meaning of independence," he said.
Anwar said Malaysians must therefore understand why colonialism was rejected in the first place, because the country did not want its systems, wealth, culture and future dictated by outsiders.
"We do not want our system to be determined by foreigners. We do not want the country's wealth to be taken by foreign rulers and brought out.
"We have our religion, our culture and our people, and they should decide," he added.
Anwar said giving meaning to independence also required Malaysia to build a nation that was united, confident and capable of determining its own direction.
He said this included giving young Malaysians greater space to express their views, participate in public discourse and contribute to national development.
Referring to reforms involving universities, Anwar said young people should not be unnecessarily constrained from expressing their views.
"If they are wrong, correct them. If they assault someone, there are laws. It does not mean freedom is unlimited. This is a country governed by the rule of law," he said.
However, he stressed that laws should not be used simply to restrict young people, arguing that a mature and independent nation must trust its citizens while maintaining accountability.
Anwar said Malaysia's future depended on a new generation that was confident in its history and identity while being prepared to embrace new technologies, artificial intelligence, digitalisation and other emerging fields.
"We have to reach for the sky, but we must also remain rooted to the ground," he said.
He said Malaysians must remain rooted in values, morality, religion, culture and humanity while pursuing economic and technological progress.
Anwar also urged Malaysians to reject corruption, abuse of power and the misuse of public resources, saying independence would have little meaning if national wealth continued to be lost through mismanagement and corruption.
He said the country's resources must instead be channelled towards improving education, strengthening institutions and raising the living standards of Malaysians.
"Why can't we look at ourselves as this great Malaysian nation, to show compassion, love and ensure that every single Malaysian benefits and is inspired?" he said.
Anwar said the younger generation now carried the responsibility of completing the work begun by previous generations by building a Malaysia that was strong, respected and dignified.
"Let us celebrate independence with pride and gratitude, and with the determination to bring meaningful change to the country," he said.
He urged young Malaysians to see Merdeka not simply as an annual celebration, but as a continuing national responsibility.
"If all young Malaysians make that commitment, yes, we will deliver," he said.

Title: Haze: Sri Aman, Serian record very unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in Sri Aman and Serian in Sarawak is deteriorating, with readings climbing into the Air Pollutant Index Management System's "very unhealthy" bracket as transboundary haze from Indonesia continues to affect parts of the country.
Sri Aman's Air Pollutant Index (API) rose from 227 at 11am to 240 at 5pm.
Similarly, Serian recorded an API reading of 228, up from 204 this morning.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.
Five other districts in Sarawak also recorded higher "unhealthy" readings.
Sarikei recorded an API of 193, Samarahan (189), Kuching (182), Mukah (171) and Sibu (166). Other areas recording unhealthy levels included Bintulu (157), Kapit (156) and Samalaju (152).
The deteriorating conditions followed a report by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC), which detected clusters of isolated to scattered fire hotspots across parts of Kalimantan, as well as southern and central Sumatra.
"Moderate to dense smoke haze was observed over the western parts of Borneo, while moderate smoke haze was observed drifting in the northwest direction from the central parts of Sumatra into the western parts of Peninsular Malaysia," the centre said in its 11am update.
The ASMC added that moderate to dense smoke plumes were also observed in other parts of Kalimantan, and central and southern Sumatra.
It warned that hotspot activity and haze conditions were expected to remain elevated across fire-prone regions experiencing dry spells, prolonging the risk of transboundary haze.
Prevailing winds over the southern Asean region were also forecast to blow from the southeast to southwest.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 161, while Batu Muda logged 156. In Putrajaya, the index stood at 155.
In Selangor, Shah Alam and Johan Setia both registered readings of 156, followed by Petaling Jaya (153), Kuala Selangor (124) and Klang (118).
In the northern region, Sungai Petani, Kedah, recorded an API of 160, while Langkawi and Alor Star registered readings of 151 and 128, respectively.
In Penang, Minden recorded an API of 158, followed closely by Seberang Perai (157) and Seberang Jaya (156).
Meanwhile, unhealthy readings were logged in Taiping (158), Tanjung Malim (156) and Tasek Ipoh (153) in Perak.
Nilai, Negri Sembilan, recorded an API of 154, while Seremban registered 151 and Segamat, Johor, logged an API reading of 129.

Title: Six Sukhois, three Airbus aircraft to highlight Melaka National Day
Article:
MELAKA: Six Sukhoi fighter jets will headline this year's state-level National Day celebration at Dataran 1Malaysia, Klebang, with the public also able to view Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) assets and capabilities.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said three Airbus air transport aircraft would also fly over Melaka, while six Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) warships would be open for public viewing.
He said the displays would give the public an opportunity to gain a closer understanding of the nation's defence capabilities.
"We extend our gratitude and appreciation to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) and the Malaysian Armed Forces as a whole for the impressive flypast involving 6 Sukhoi fighter jets and three Airbus air transport aircraft.
"This collaboration has given the people of Melaka an opportunity to witness the capabilities and professionalism of our security forces," he told reporters after observing the full rehearsal for the celebration at Dataran 1Malaysia, Klebang, here today.
On preparations for the National Day celebration on Aug 31, Ab Rauf said he was satisfied with the performance and commitment demonstrated by all parties during the full rehearsal.
He said a total of 158 contingents comprising 8,531 personnel would take part in this year's parade, while 11 floats and 21 vehicles, accompanied by 627 personnel, would further enliven the festivities.
The celebration is expected to draw more than 50,000 visitors.
Ab Rauf also said 15 tourist attractions across Melaka would offer free admission to the public on Aug 31.
He said the initiative was among special measures introduced by the state government in conjunction with National Day to allow the public to enjoy the various attractions available in the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for KL, Selangor and five states until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in six states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today.
MetMalaysia said the warning covered the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, as well as Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.
The two other states affected are Selangor, covering Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Petaling, and Johor, covering Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi and Segamat.

Title: Haze: Asthma, conjunctivitis cases on the rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma cases in the country have surged amid deteriorating air quality caused by the haze affecting several areas nationwide, with 1,811 cases recorded during epidemiological week (EW) 34 (Aug 23-29), compared with 219 cases in the previous week.
The Health Ministry (MOH), in a statement today, said the figures were based on surveillance data from sentinel facilities.
It said cases of conjunctivitis also rose to 720 from 146 in EW 33, while acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) fell by 50 per cent, from 3,674 to 1,857 cases.
"No deaths linked to complications arising from the haze have been reported. However, monitoring through the National Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC) has been stepped up," the statement said.
On air quality, the MOH said 30 of the 68 Air Pollutant Index (API) monitoring stations recorded unhealthy or very unhealthy readings as of 8am today, with Sri Aman, Sarawak recording the highest reading of 222, classified as very unhealthy.
Other states and federal territories recording unhealthy API readings were Perak, Kedah, Penang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perlis, Johor, Putrajaya and Kuala Lumpur.
Following the rise in respiratory-related illnesses, the ministry advised the public, particularly high-risk groups such as children, senior citizens and those with chronic lung conditions, to limit outdoor physical activities.
The public is also advised to wear suitable masks, such as N95 masks, when outdoors and to drink plenty of water to stay hydrated.
"Seek immediate medical attention at the nearest health facility if you experience breathing difficulties, persistent coughing or eye irritation," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wajah Malaysia puts Malaysians in the picture
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians can become part of a nationwide mosaic of faces set to appear on billboards, in newspapers and on television through the Wajah Malaysia campaign.
At the heart of the campaign is a mobile roadshow truck — a moving hub equipped with a photobooth and activities that will stop at key locations throughout the National Day celebrations.
Currently stationed at Dataran Merdeka alongside Festival Ambang Merdeka 2026, the truck allows visitors to step into the photobooth and see themselves featured on a personalised mock front page of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian or Harian Metro.
The campaign aims to collect more than 600 photographs, which will be brought together to form mosaics to be featured on billboards, in newspapers and on television on Malaysia Day on Sept 16.
NSTP head of Branding and Intellectual Property Tengku Kaifimirza Tuan Cherit@Tengku Hamzah said the campaign provided an opportunity to engage with Malaysians, particularly younger visitors gathering at Dataran Merdeka.
"We want to promote our brands to the public and show that we are still very much present in the market," he told the New Straits Times.
He said Dataran Merdeka was an ideal location to reach younger Malaysians, with school groups from as far as Kedah and Johor among those visiting ahead of National Day.
"Just now, more than 50 students from Kedah came with their teachers just to celebrate National Day.
"You can see a lot of young people coming here," he said.
The mobile roadshow truck will head to the Petronas Twin Towers early tomorrow morning to reach marathon participants before returning to Dataran Merdeka at noon.
Visitors will also receive copies of NSTP newspapers, with 900 copies distributed daily — 300 each of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian and Harian Metro.
They can also take part in activities to win T-shirts, souvenirs and exclusive Media Prima merchandise.
The Wajah Malaysia campaign is a collaboration between the NSTP Marketing Department and Media Prima Group Marketing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's bonsai industry poised for global growth, says Nga
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's pool of world-class bonsai expertise represents a significant and largely untapped opportunity to elevate the craft beyond a recreational pastime into a more professional and commercially viable industry, capitalising on rising international demand.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the country already possessed all the foundational elements required to transform bonsai into a high-value economic activity.
These include a deep reservoir of specialised knowledge, rich biodiversity, a talented community of bonsai artists and growing global interest in the art form.
Speaking on the sector's potential, Nga said that under the National Landscape Industry Master Plan, Malaysia's bonsai and landscape industry currently generates an estimated RM40 billion in annual economic value, with strong prospects for further expansion.
"Our bonsai ecosystem needs to evolve from passion to production, from expertise to enterprise, and from hobby to industry, for us to be better recognised globally," he said at the launch of the 10th World Bonsai Convention 2026 at Pavilion Bukit Jalil here today.
Nga said the growing presence of overseas collectors from Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, India and Singapore seeking finished bonsai specimens and raw planting materials was clear evidence that international demand was already firmly established.
However, he said the sector had yet to realise its full potential, largely due to the limited supply of high-quality bonsai.
Nga observed that countries such as Japan, China, Taiwan and South Korea had developed bonsai beyond individual collections into comprehensive ecosystems encompassing cultivation, nurseries, training programmes, exhibitions, tourism, trade and international exports.
Malaysia, he said, had a strong foundation to develop a similar ecosystem.
The Housing and Local Government Ministry, through the National Landscape Department, was prepared to strengthen collaboration with bonsai associations, practitioners and industry stakeholders.
These efforts, he said, would include exploring opportunities to integrate bonsai more deeply into Malaysia's broader landscape, horticultural and creative industry framework, covering cultivation techniques, skills development, branding strategies, tourism linkages and international promotional campaigns.
"We want Malaysian bonsai to be admired not only for its beauty, but also recognised for its value in the knowledge we preserve, the artists we empower, the entrepreneurs we create and the new opportunities we generate for Malaysians," he said.
Nga said the convention, held once every four years and hosted by Malaysia for the first time, drew participants from more than 40 countries.
He described the event as a potential launchpad for the next chapter of Malaysia's bonsai ecosystem, offering a strategic platform to catalyse further industry growth.
He also highlighted that Malaysia's bonsai community had continued to thrive since the establishment of the Malaysia Bonsai and Suiseki Society in 1988.
Today, more than 10 bonsai associations are active nationwide, reflecting the craft's expanding reach and vibrancy across the country.
Over the past three decades, local practitioners have steadily refined their techniques and deepened their expertise, reinforcing Malaysia's standing as an emerging regional hub for bonsai development, knowledge exchange and commercial trade.
